--- ABSTRACT ---
[BACKGROUND]: Interferon Lambda-3 (IFN-λ3) gene polymorphism is associated with spontaneous clearance of hepatitis C virus (HCV) and response to IFN-based therapy (IFN). However, very few data are available about its value in predicting sustained virologic response (SVR) in patients with cirrhosis, and whether IFN-λ3 genotype influences liver disease progression remains unclear.
[METHODS]: We determined IFN-λ3 genotype by PCR in a cohort of patients with compensated HCV-related cirrhosis, enrolled between 1989 and 1992. Person-years follow-up was calculated for each individual from the date of enrolment to the development of first episode of decompensation, HCC, liver transplant, death or end of follow-up. The follow-up of patients who achieved SVR was censored at the time of IFN initiation. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression analyses were used to assess the association between IFN-λ3 genotype and clinical outcome.
[RESULTS]: IFN-λ3 was determined in 264 patients (52% males, mean age 57±8 years, 67% HCV genotype (G)1, while CC, CT and TT genotypes were 36%, 50% and 14%, respectively. During a median follow-up of 14.8 years, 149 (56%) patients received IFN. Overall, SVR was achieved in 31 (21%) patients, 40% among those with CC genotype (22% in G1 and 61% in G2, respectively) compared to 10% and 13% among patients with CT and TT genotypes (p<0.0001). Univariate and multivariate analyses found no association between IFN-λ3 (CC vs. non-CC genotype) and disease progression.
[CONCLUSION]: IFN-λ3 determination is fundamental for allocating cirrhotic patients to be treated with IFN, while it has no value in predicting the outcome of the disease.

key_findings.finding: The cohort included 264 patients with compensated HCV-related cirrhosis, enrolled in 1989–1992; 52% were male, mean age was 57±8 years, and 67% had HCV genotype 1. source_tools.relevance: Full abstract gives sample size, baseline characteristics, genotype distribution, enrollment period, treatment exposure, and follow-up duration.

key_findings.finding: The prespecified clinical endpoint was time to first decompensation, hepatocellular carcinoma, liver transplantation, death, or end of follow-up; follow-up for patients achieving SVR was censored at interferon initiation.

source_tools.relevance: Methods abstract explicitly defines the composite clinical outcome and censoring rule.

key_findings.finding: Overall SVR was 31/149 treated patients (21%); SVR was 40% in CC patients versus 10% in CT and 13% in TT patients (p<0.0001), with genotype-specific CC SVR of 22% in HCV genotype 1 and 61% in genotype 2. source_tools.relevance: Abstract provides the SVR counts, genotype-stratified percentages, p-value, and the adjusted/unadjusted disease-progression conclusion.

key_findings.finding: The paper concludes that IFNL3 genotype is useful for allocating cirrhotic patients to interferon treatment because it predicts treatment response, but it has no value for predicting long-term clinical outcome.
